summary: This Dockerfile creates a Ubuntu container with the eza file-listing tool installed and configured with a custom alias. It sets up a demo directory with various file types to showcase eza's output, customizes the bash prompt to show a container indicator, and starts an interactive bash shell.

explanations.3: This tells apt-get to skip interactive prompts during installation, preventing the build from hanging if a package asks for user input.
explanations.5: The && chains commands together so they run sequentially, and the backslash lets us continue the command on the next line for readability.
explanations.9: After installing packages, we delete the apt cache files to reduce the final image size—we won't need them again after installation.
explanations.14: The curl flags -fsSL mean: fail on errors, silent mode, show errors, and follow redirects—standard for reliable downloads in Docker.
explanations.16: We pipe the downloaded tar.gz file directly to tar to extract it, and -C /usr/local/bin tells tar to extract into the system binary directory so eza is available everywhere.
explanations.19: We're appending to /root/.bashrc so that every time bash starts, it redefines the 'ls' command to actually run 'eza' with those specific formatting options.
explanations.24: We create the directory structure with -p, which means 'create parent directories too' so the whole path /root/demo/src and /root/demo/docs gets built in one command.
explanations.33: The PS1 variable controls the bash prompt appearance; this one adds a whale emoji, colors the username in cyan, and makes it clear you're inside a container.
explanations.35: The -i flag makes bash interactive (accepting user input) rather than just executing a script and exiting.
